world.bio: Year 3 teacher at a state primary in Mt Roskill, Auckland. My class has kids from fourteen countries and about half don't speak English at home. I keep a shoebox of picture cards for newcomers and have been teaching for eight years, the last four here. Outside school I'm renovating a leaky villa with my partner and playing netball on Thursday nights.
skills_assets: Eight years of primary teaching, four with a high-ESOL class
A shoebox of about 200 hand-drawn picture cards for newcomers
Basic te reo Māori and some Samoan classroom phrases
Class blog the parents actually read
A villa in Sandringham with half the windows replaced

projects.name: Newcomer buddy system
projects.text: Pairing each new child with a Year 5 buddy who speaks the same language, where possible. Works well for Samoan and Hindi. Doesn't work yet for the two Korean kids and doesn't exist for a Mandarin buddy.

projects.name: Villa renovation
projects.text: Leaky windows, 1920s villa. Replaced front windows in August, back ones next month. The builder keeps changing the schedule. Budget is the real villain.

notes.text: Term 3 is flying. Tui's reading level jumped a whole band. She read the whole 'Kiwi the Brave' page and then asked if she could read it to the class. I nearly cried.
Teaching notes: 'New boy from China hasn't said a word in three weeks — eats lunch alone by the fence'. Tried the picture cards, he points but doesn't speak. Not sure if he's shy or just waiting.

Staff meeting. Principal says the ESOL budget was cut this year, so we have no Mandarin-speaking teacher aide this term. We've got Samoan and Hindi support, nothing else. Asked if there are any relief funds. Maybe, she said.
Netball, lost by two. Our goal shooter rolled her ankle. I've been playing wing defence like it's 2012 and my knees are not in on the joke.
Villa: the builder says the back windows are delayed to mid-November. Water coming in the laundry again. Put a bucket there, named it Gerald.
Dad's hip replacement went well. He called me from the ward and complained about the food. That's the old Dad. Mum is furious that he's already trying to walk without the frame.
Tried drawing the lunch cards with simple Chinese characters next to the picture. Looked up '吃饭' and '朋友'. No idea if the pronunciation is right. The new boy looked at them and smiled, once.
Parent-teacher day. Two parents asked about their kids' reading, one asked if the school can run a homework club. I don't have the time. Might ask the principal.
Holidays soon. Sleeping in. Maybe sand the villa's floors if I'm brave. The new boy has started drawing a house with a very big dog in front of it.

messages.text: Ben: builder called, wants another 3k for the window frames. Hana: for the same windows? Ben: apparently the timber went up. Hana: I'm going to scream into a pillow.
Principal: I've put your request for a Mandarin aide in the budget meeting. Hana: Thank you. Principal: No promises. Hana: Understood.
Meera: Did you see the new boy at lunch? Hana: Yes, he sits by the fence. Meera: I tried to sit with him, he moved. Hana: He's not unfriendly, he's waiting.
Dad: The nurse here is called Rosa and she laughs at my jokes. Hana: Don't flirt with the nurses. Dad: I'm 68, I can flirt.
Mum: Can you come Saturday? Hana: Yes, I'll bring lunch. Mum: He's walking without the frame again. Hana: Tell him I said no.

relations.about: Partner, a plumber's apprentice, organised, slightly stressed about money.
Fair, but squeezed by the budget.
Live in Papakura; Dad just had a hip replacement.

constraints: No spare weekday evenings during term
Cannot spend personal money on school resources more than about $50 a term
Class admin takes the lunch hour; no flexible time in the school day
Children's names and photos stay inside the school system
sensitive: The villa budget is blowing out and the couple have talked about selling
Worries she is not doing enough for the quiet new boy
Fatigue: got sick twice this term and still came in
